title: Pre-faith actual remission would void gospel conditions and contradict alien enmity (Col 1:21; 1 John 3)
source_text: XVIII. Ac profecto si ante fidem & conversionem electis peccata actu remissa essent, frustra & sine ratione Scriptura proponeret fidem & poenitentiam, tanquam conditionem sub qua nobis offertur remissio peccatorum, & sine qua illam consequi non possumus. Adde quod ille cui peccata remissa sunt pacem habet cum Deo, & est ipsi reconciliatus. At quomodo hoc convenire potest illis qui sunt adhuc a Deo alienati, & inimici ejus mente & operibus malis? Qualis fidelium & electorum ipsorum ante vocationem & conversionem suam, conditio describitur ab Apostolo Paulo, Coloss. 1. 21. Denique Scriptura sacra beatum praedicat illum cujus tecta sunt peccata, & iniquitates remissae. Sed quis praedicare audebit beatum eum qui adhuc peccatum faciens, nondum ex Deo, sed ex Diabolo est, & charitate vacuus, ac fratrem odio habens, vitam aeternam non habet in seipso manentem, nec translatus est de morte ad vitam, teste Apostolo Joanne Epistolae primae capite tertio? Qui facit peccatum, inquit, ex Diabolo est. Item, Omnis qui non facit justitiam non est ex Deo, & qui non diligit fratrem suum. Et, Qui non diligit manet in morte.
pass_a_gloss: And indeed if before faith and conversion sins were actually remitted to the elect, Scripture would in vain and without reason propose faith and repentance as the condition under which remission of sins is offered to us, and without which we cannot obtain it. Add that he to whom sins have been remitted has peace with God and is reconciled to him. But how can this agree with those who are still alienated from God and enemies of him in mind and evil works?—which condition of the faithful and elect themselves before their calling and conversion is described by the Apostle Paul (Col. 1:21). Finally sacred Scripture proclaims blessed the one whose sins are covered and whose iniquities are remitted. But who will dare proclaim blessed him who, still doing sin, is not yet of God but of the Devil, and empty of charity, and hating his brother, does not have eternal life abiding in himself, nor has been translated from death to life, as the Apostle John testifies in the third chapter of the first Epistle? Whoever does sin, he says, is of the Devil. Likewise, Everyone who does not do righteousness is not of God, and who does not love his brother. And, Whoever does not love remains in death.
pass_b_english: If elect already had actual pardon pre-faith, gospel conditions of faith/repentance would be empty.
Col 1:21 enmity and 1 John 3’s ‘still in death’ cannot be called blessed covered-sin status.
